important.name: Roast skip drops the linear pass for unbucketed paths, unlike the tested arm
important.summary:
The catalog row's skip_lenses ["roast"] removes the linear docstring-vs-code pass from the roast slot entirely. When the roast slot replaces OVERALL (below SMALL_PR_FILES), no slot runs the pass on unbucketed paths. The stated rationale only covers bucketed paths: "every bucketed path already gets the pass from its bucket slot". Unbucketed is not limited to manifests in a generic plugin. review_bucket treats any file whose suffix is not in _RUNTIME_SUFFIXES (.go, .rs, .java, .yaml, non-schema .json) as unbucketed, so such code gets no docstring pass at all on a small roast PR. The experiment in docs/RESEARCH/pr-review/0203_roast_slot_duration.md measured arm C, which kept the pass for unbucketed paths, not a full drop. SKILL.md:258-259 and the catalog's policy.small_pr still say the roast slot keeps OVERALL's coverage, and that is no longer true for these paths.

Also (roast): On a PR under 20 files where the roast roll fires, roast replaces OVERALL (review_plan.py:519-523), and `skip_lenses: ["roast"]` now strips the linear docstring-vs-code pass from it (review_plan.py:344-356). Bucketed paths still get the pass from their bucket slot, but unbucketed paths get it from nobody: no OVERALL slot exists and no bucket owns them. The research note's arm C, the only measured variant of this cut, limited the pass to unbucketed paths rather than removing it (0203_roast_slot_duration.md:83), so the shipped behavior is stricter than anything measured. The catalog's own `policy.small_pr` (line 50) still promises the roast slot keeps OVERALL's coverage and "only the duplicate slot is dropped". This PR is a live example: `CrossCuttingLensCatalog.json`, the most prose-contract-heavy file in it, is unbucketed. The data says "saved a quarter"; the contract says "coverage kept". Only one of those is still true.

Also (skill_package): The catalog row's summary and trigger description (CrossCuttingLensCatalog.json 7, 9) now read 'every reviewer slot except the roast slot' with no pr-review qualifier, but the catalog is shared with pr-team, whose orchestrator (agents/pr-team-orchestrator.md 224-228) writes 'the mandatory linear sub-lens instructions' into the prompt of EACH planned reviewer, its dice-gated harness:roast-my-code slot included. skip_lenses is read only by harness_lib.review_plan (pr-review), so the two skills now disagree about the same catalog row without either saying so.

Also (system_shape): policy.small_pr (CrossCuttingLensCatalog.json:50) says the roast slot replacing OVERALL on a small PR keeps 'OVERALL's full scope ... so coverage is kept'. With skip_lenses ['roast'] (catalog:13) that slot no longer runs the linear docstring-vs-code pass, and on a small PR it is the only slot that holds the unbucketed paths (review_plan.py:519-523, slot_plan docstring at 540-541). The stated rationale (catalog:9, SKILL.md:237-238: 'every bucketed path already gets the pass from its bucket slot') is true only for bucketed paths; the research note (0203_roast_slot_duration.md:130-131) accepted the gap because the measured unbucketed paths were manifests, but no published doc states it.

Also (runtime, roast): sub_lenses_for (review_plan.py:344-351) applies the catalog's new skip_lenses ["roast"], so the roast slot never gets the linear docstring-vs-code pass. The catalog's reason is that every bucketed path already gets the pass from its bucket slot. Unbucketed paths (plain .json, .yaml, .toml and similar) have no bucket slot, though, and on a small PR the roast slot replaces OVERALL as their only reviewer. Whether those paths get the pass now depends on the 50/50 roast roll. This contradicts policy.small_pr's statement that 'coverage is kept' when the roast replaces OVERALL.

Also (runtime): _skipped_lenses (review_plan.py:354-356) resolves each skip_lenses entry with resolve_lens, which keeps an unknown name as a plain string instead of rejecting it. A project default_sub_lenses row that names a slot id such as "config" (the config-or-registry slot id, which is neither a member value nor a member name), or a lens name with a typo, matches no slot and skips nothing, with no error. _merge_catalog validates project lenses but not the skip_lenses of project sub-lenses.

Also (roast): `_skipped_lenses` (review_plan.py:354-356) runs each entry through `resolve_lens`, which returns any unrecognized string unchanged. A project row with `skip_lenses: ["roasts"]` or a lens name that does not exist resolves to a plain string that matches no slot, so the row runs everywhere and nothing complains. `_merge_catalog` validates project lenses through `_check_project_lens` but never looks at default_sub_lenses rows. The enums were added to stop free-form strings drifting, and this new key is a free-form string.
fix: Keep the linear pass in the roast slot for the slot's unbucketed paths only (arm C): sub_lenses_for or lens_section emits the linear template with a pointer limiting it to the paths review_bucket returns UNBUCKETED for, and drops it only when there are none.

Keep the full drop and say so: add to the catalog row's trigger.description, policy.small_pr and SKILL.md lines 233-239 / 258-259 that on a small roast PR unbucketed paths get no linear pass, and name in the research Outcome that the adopted cut is wider than arm C.

Match arm C: keep the linear pass in the roast slot but scope its template to the slot's unbucketed paths (for example `sub_lenses_for` returns the row with a path filter, and `lens_section` appends `Apply it only to: <unbucketed paths>` when the roast slot carries any).
Skip the pass for roast only when an OVERALL slot runs beside it (large PR), and keep it on the small-PR roast slot that replaces OVERALL.

If the gap is accepted, amend `policy.small_pr` and the SKILL.md 'Default sub-lens' paragraph to state that a roast-rolled small PR gives unbucketed paths no linear pass, and record that in the research note's Outcome.
Qualify the catalog row: 'pr-review: every reviewer slot except the roast slot (skip_lenses); pr-team: every reviewer' in the summary or trigger description.
Or make pr-team honor the row: amend pr-team-orchestrator.md 228 to skip the linear sub-lens for the harness:roast-my-code slot per the row's skip_lenses.
Add the exception to policy.small_pr and to the rationale at catalog:9 / SKILL.md:237-238: 'unbucketed paths get no linear pass when roast replaces OVERALL'.
Or keep the pass for unbucketed paths only in the roast slot (filter its sub-lens scope to PathBucket.UNBUCKETED paths) so the coverage claim holds.

Run the sub-lens in the roast slot when it replaces OVERALL (small PR): skip it only for the side-by-side roast slot, for example by planning the small-PR roast with a flag that sub_lenses_for checks, or by skipping only when the slot plan also holds an OVERALL slot.
Alternatively, restrict the skip to bucketed paths: keep the pass in the roast brief and limit it to the slot's unbucketed paths, and update the catalog trigger description to say so.

In _merge_catalog, check that each project default_sub_lenses row's skip_lenses entries resolve to a PathBucket, Lens or ScopeLens member or name a catalog project lens, and raise ValueError otherwise, as _check_project_lens does for lens names.
Alternatively, have _MissStrEnum._missing_ also match a member's slot_id so that "config" resolves to PathBucket.CFG, and still raise on names that resolve to nothing.

In `_merge_catalog`, check each project default_sub_lenses row: every `skip_lenses` entry must resolve to a `PathBucket`/`Lens`/`ScopeLens` member or name a lens in the merged catalog; otherwise raise `ValueError` naming the row (load_lens_catalog already turns that into a capture error).

minor.name: ls-tree output is matched unquoted, so non-ASCII skill paths are missed
minor.summary: skill_folders_at_head runs `git ls-tree -r --name-only` without -z (pr_review.py:383) and compares each output line exactly with `<folder>SKILL.md` (review_plan.py:235-238). With the default core.quotePath, git wraps paths that hold non-ASCII or special characters in quotes and escapes them. A skill folder with such a name therefore never matches, and its per-skill-package lens does not fire.
fix: Pass -z to ls-tree and split the output on "\0" instead of calling splitlines(): `git_out(repo, "ls-tree", "-r", "-z", "--name-only", head, "--", *files).split("\0")`.

minor.name: Brief lists skill names only, though discovery now spans every skills/ root
minor.summary: lens_paths now finds skills under any skills/<name>/ folder (for example plugins/harness/skills and plugins/arc-straps/skills), then dedupes the triggered list by bare name (pr_review.py:408). The brief prints only those names (review_briefs.py:220-221). When two roots hold a skill with the same name, both folders trigger the lens, since a same-name folder counts as a mention, but the brief shows one name. Nothing tells the reviewer which folder `<name>` refers to.
fix: Carry the triggered folders, not only the names, into BriefContext.skills (or a parallel field), and print each as `name (folder)` on the 'Triggered skills' line.
Alternatively, keep one entry per folder when names collide, for example by dropping the dict.fromkeys name dedupe and printing the folder path.

The reason given at :237-238 ("every bucketed path already gets the pass") deliberately leaves them out, but the cut paragraph still promises full coverage.

minor.name: "project default sub-lenses carry no skip" is a default, not a rule
minor.summary:
SKILL.md:239 says a project's own default sub-lenses "carry no skip and reach every slot". `_merge_catalog` (review_plan.py:313-314) copies project `default_sub_lenses` rows as they are, and `sub_lenses_for` (review_plan.py:344-351) applies `skip_lenses` to every row, project rows included. No lens-file check rejects the key. So a project row that sets `skip_lenses` is skipped in the slots it names. The sentence reads as a guarantee the code does not give.

Also (skill_package): SKILL.md 231-239 labels the linear docstring-vs-code pass mandatory with no skip path, then justifies the roast skip with 'every bucketed path already gets the pass from its bucket slot'. Unbucketed paths (SKILL.md 223: 'reviewed by OVERALL only', e.g. plugin.json manifests, .yaml, .toml) have no bucket slot. Under the small-PR cut (SKILL.md 258-259, review_plan.py 520-523) a roast roll replaces OVERALL with a ScopeLens.ROAST slot, and sub_lenses_for (review_plan.py 344-351) filters the linear row out of it, so on a sub-20-file PR with a roast roll no slot runs the pass over unbucketed paths. The SKILL.md claim 'coverage is kept' for that cut no longer holds for this sub-lens, and tests/lib/test_review_roast_sub_lens.py covers only runtime and tests paths.

Also (skill_package): SKILL.md 239 states 'a project's own default sub-lenses carry no skip and reach every slot'. _merge_catalog (review_plan.py 313-314) appends project default_sub_lenses unvalidated and sub_lenses_for / _skipped_lenses (review_plan.py 344-356) honor a skip_lenses key on any row, project rows included; the test module docstring (tests/lib/test_review_roast_sub_lens.py 6-7) says as much ('unless their rows say otherwise'). The catalog's policy.project_lenses text does not mention skip_lenses for project rows either, so a project author has no documented way to learn the key exists.

Also (overall): SKILL.md:239 says "a project's own default sub-lenses carry no skip and reach every slot". _merge_catalog appends project default_sub_lenses rows verbatim, and sub_lenses_for / _skipped_lenses (review_plan.py:344-356) honor skip_lenses on any row, so a project row that sets skip_lenses does not reach every slot. tests/lib/test_review_roast_sub_lens.py:6-7 describes the actual behavior: rows reach roast "unless their rows say otherwise". The plan wording (TASK-3 step 3) has the same overstatement.

Also (system_shape): pr-review SKILL.md:238 states 'a project's own default sub-lenses carry no skip and reach every slot', and PIP TASK-3 step 3 (0007 PIP:146) says 'project rows carry none'. minor.name: per-skill-package row narrows the grep roots the driver actually searches
minor.summary: SKILL.md:246 says `<name>` must appear under `.claude`, `docs`, `.github` or "that skill root's top folder". The driver computes one root set for every skill: plugins/harness/scripts/pr_review.py:405 calls `rp.skill_grep_roots(folders)` over all touched skill folders, and review_plan.py:246-249 adds every folder's top segment. With skills under `.claude/skills/x/` and `plugins/h/skills/y/`, skill `x` is also searched under `plugins/`, so a mention there triggers the lens even though the table says it should not. The effect is an extra slot, never a missed one, but the table no longer describes the trigger exactly.
fix: Reword the row to "... under `.claude`, `docs`, `.github` or the top folder of any touched skill root, outside the skill's own folder".
Search each folder's own roots instead: in `lens_paths` pass `rp.skill_grep_roots((f,))` per folder rather than one shared `roots`, which matches the current table text.

No such comparison exists at the head; the guard just would not catch one.

fix: Scan `[node.left, *node.comparators]` instead of `node.comparators` in the loop at line 133.
Keep `_MOVED` for the driver-absence check and add the library names (`draft_json`, `role`, `scope_text`) to the `hasattr(rb, ...)` assertion, e.g. via an old-to-new mapping.
